title: The Deadline and the Team — An Unfolding Story
synopsis: Ten days to deliver. Your best specialist is exhausted, your newest colleague wants to help, and a director wants certainty you do not have.

opening.speaker: Malik Thompson
opening.title: The Stand-up Erupts
opening.text: Malik misses a handoff and snaps, “I'm doing the work of three people.” Other employees look down at their desks while the Friday work queue grows.
opening.prompt: How do you handle the missed handoff and Malik's warning?

choices.text: Acknowledge the missed handoff, check on Malik privately, and audit the distribution of work.
choices.reaction: Malik shares the real backlog, Hannah receives a safe learning task, and the team starts flagging risks earlier.
choices.coaching: Protect sustainable performance; attend to both task and relationship.

choices.text: Thank Malik for the honesty, then ask everyone to push through until Friday.
choices.reaction: A temporary sense of calm leaves important ownership and quality questions unresolved.
choices.coaching: A reassuring or incomplete answer may delay an uncomfortable issue, but does not remove responsibility.

choices.text: Criticize Malik for the tone and order the team to work harder.
choices.reaction: Employees become reluctant to report overload, and preventable defects begin stacking up.
choices.coaching: Silencing evidence or substituting certainty for verification increases human and operational risk.

critical-decision.speaker: Cameron Brooks
critical-decision.title: The Director Calls
critical-decision.text: Cameron asks, “Are you promising the complete deliverable by Friday?” Nora's figures show that is possible only with reduced scope or new capacity.
critical-decision.prompt: What forecast and recommendation will you provide?

choices.text: Offer Cameron a verified forecast, a reduced-scope option, and a staffing decision with checkpoints.

fallout-recovery.title: A Preventable Rework Loop
fallout-recovery.text: An unchecked handoff produces defects and two workers volunteer to stay late. The original target is no longer credible.

ending-strong.speaker: Narrator
ending-strong.title: Ending: Trust and Direction
ending-strong.text: The revised plan meets critical needs without concealing risk. Malik receives sustainable support, Hannah learns safely, and the team owns its handoffs.
ending-strong.reflection: Which observable behaviors made this result possible, and how will you repeat them?

ending-fragile.speaker: Narrator
ending-fragile.title: Ending: A Recoverable Gap
ending-fragile.text: Some work ships, but the team remains stretched and the forecast requires repair. People are watching whether you follow through.
ending-fragile.reflection: Which assumption or handoff would you revisit before the next decision?

ending-damaged.speaker: Narrator
ending-damaged.title: Ending: A Costly Leadership Pattern
ending-damaged.text: The team misses an avoidable defect, burnout worsens, and Cameron learns the true position too late. A credible recovery plan is now essential.
ending-damaged.reflection: What would you acknowledge, repair and change first to prevent repetition?
